brief: Bitcoin has lost roughly a quarter of its value since October 21. A weekend flush triggered near $2 billion in liquidations after BTC broke below its 200-day moving average around $73,000. ETF outflows have run seven straight days, with $2.35 billion leaving spot BTC ETFs over the last two weeks. MARA sold 13,597 BTC, about $1.1 billion, in six weeks, 40% of its September-end holdings, using $750 million to repay Bitcoin-backed loans and signaling future sales toward AI data-center funding. It has sold over 40,000 BTC in 2026. Bitcoin is again trading below Strategy's average purchase price, raising doubt over whether Strategy can keep bidding while others sell. Funding turned negative on Binance, OKX and Bybit on November 13, meaning traders increasingly pay to hold shorts. The note floats a theory, citing the SpaceX IPO precedent (BTC fell 19% in the 50 days before it versus a similar 18% decline now before Anthropic's), that investors are selling Bitcoin to fund Anthropic IPO allocations, calling it possible capital rotation into AI. It also notes NVDA's six-week losing streak, longest since 2012, and Chinese equities red 13 of the last 14 weeks, framing Bitcoin's drop as reconnecting with weak risk assets.
